newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan firms' profits capped by Sumitomo, utilities.
newsitem.headline: Japan firms' profits capped by Sumitomo, utilities.

text.p: Poor earnings by electric power companies and scandal-hit Sumitomo Corp are expected to cap first-half profit increases by big Japanese firms, a research institute said on Thursday.

Hiroki Matsushita, an analyst of Wako Research Institute of Economics, said big Japanese firms are likely to show an average year-on-year increase of less than 10 percent in their parent current profit in the six months to September 30, due to profit declines at the electric power companies.
He also said the results would be further squeezed by a huge half-year net loss posted by trading house Sumitomo.

Wako Research said on Thursday that half-year current profits posted by large firms as of Wednesday showed an average increase of 11.1 percent, with post-tax profits growing four percent. Wako Research based its figures on interim parent results released so far by 646 companies. Wako Research tracks 766 companies and expects the average profit increase to fall below 10 percent when they all report their results.

Current profit is pretax and includes gains or losses on non-operating activities, while net profit is obtained by subtracting extraordinary profit or losses from current earnings and then deducting income tax.
Before Sumitomo and the electric power companies announced their results this week, the average increase in first-half current profits was more than 14 percent.
Sumitomo said it posted a parent net loss of 212.60 billion yen ($1.91 billion) in the first half of 1996/97, against a net profit of 7.62 billion yen ($68.6 million) in the same period a year ago.
The trading house fired its chief copper trader Yasuo Hamanaka in June and accused him of racking up losses, now estimated at $2.6 billion, on unauthorised trades.

On Wednesday, Tokyo Electric Power Co Inc and two other electric power companies reported smaller half-year current profits, due mainly to a power rate cut earlier this year. Kansai Electric Power Co Inc said on Thursday that its half-year parent current profit fell 14.5 percent from a year earlier to 54.08 billion yen ($487 million).
The majority of Japan's large companies are expected to announce their half-year business results by the end of November. ($1=111 yen)
